text: dsh-driftwatch 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的会话行为比较插件，可在 DSH 中注册 drift_compare 和 drift_list 两个工具，也提供独立命令行程序。它读取两份会话日志，汇总工具调用顺序和频次、文件路径、推理量、重试、耗时等变化，并生成带分数和差异明细的 Markdown、JSON 或独立 HTML 报告；还可按阈值作为 CI 门禁。用户可按会话 ID、ID 前缀或路径指定日志，也可列出本机可比较的会话。适合排查模型、提示词或插件更新后的行为变化。运行需要 Node.js 22 及本地 DSH 会话文件，不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-driftwatch compares two DSH session logs and reports behavior drift. Its DSH tools compare sessions and list local logs; the CLI also fingerprints a session. Reports summarize tool calls, file changes, retries, and timing in Markdown, JSON, or HTML. Requires Node.js 22 and local session logs.
想比较升级模型前后的 DSH 会话表现。
帮我看两个 agent 运行记录里的工具调用差异。
DSH 能不能把行为变化整理成一份报告？
我想给会话漂移设阈值，超出时让 CI 失败。
查一下两次运行分别修改了哪些文件、用了哪些工具。
怎么快速找到本机可用于对比的 DSH 会话？
Compare two DSH runs and summarize how their behavior changed.
I need a CI check that fails when session behavior drifts past a threshold.
Show me the differences in tool calls, timing, retries, and files between two agent sessions.
dsh-driftwatch 的功能「会话行为对比」：比较两份会话日志，汇总工具序列、工具使用量、推理指标和文件操作差异，并计算漂移分数。通过 DSH 的 drift_compare 工具或 CLI compare 命令触发。
dsh-driftwatch 的功能「多格式报告」：将会话差异整理为可读摘要和明细，可输出 Markdown、JSON 或独立 HTML 文件，便于查看或附在 CI 产物中。通过 CLI compare 的格式选项触发。
dsh-driftwatch 的功能「会话列表」：按修改时间从新到旧列出本机可比较的 DSH 会话及其工作区、大小和时间。可通过 DSH 的 drift_list 工具或 CLI list 命令触发。
dsh-driftwatch 的功能「单会话指纹」：提取一份会话的工具调用、消息、耗时、重试及文件操作等行为摘要。通过 CLI fingerprint 命令触发，可输出文本或 JSON。
dsh-driftwatch README · dsh-driftwatch：**You changed a prompt, a plugin or a model. Something feels different. This tells you what actually changed — and by how much.**

dsh-driftwatch README · When you need this：- The agent behaves differently after an upgrade and you cannot point at the reason
- You want a CI gate that fails when behaviour drifts, rather than an assertion you have to write first
- You need to compare a run against a known-good run without reading 50,000 log lines

The drift score is four weighted groups, and every raw number behind them is printed — so you can disagree with the weights instead of trusting them.

You changed a prompt, a plugin, or a model. Something feels different. But *what* changed — and by how much?

DriftWatch reads two session logs and tells you exactly how the agent's behavior diverged: tool-call sequence, tool mix, file targets, reasoning volume, retries, timing. Zero dependencies. CI-ready.

> 中文文档见 [README.zh.md](README.zh.md)。

dsh-driftwatch README · The problem：DSH logs everything (`Model-visible means logged`), so the evidence already exists — but reading a 59 MB trajectory by hand is not a workflow. Existing tools solve adjacent problems:

dsh-driftwatch README · The problem：| Tool | Answers |
|---|---|
| `dsh-replay` | "show me this trajectory" (debugging) |
| `dsh-eval-harness` | "does this match my written expectations?" (assertions) |
| `dsh-session-snapshot` | "record this session so tests can rely on it" (fixtures) |
| `dsh-windtunnel` | "replay the pipeline with a scripted model" (deterministic contracts) |
| **`dsh-driftwatch`** | **"how does this run differ from that run?" (comparison)** |

dsh-driftwatch README · The problem：`dsh-replay` diffs trajectories for debugging; `dsh-eval-harness` gates on assertions written in
advance. Neither answers the question in between: *this run took a different path — is that a
problem?* DriftWatch deliberately does **not** assert and does **not** render trajectories. It
produces a *drift report*: a structured, reviewable statement of behavioral change, plus an
optional threshold gate for CI.

dsh-driftwatch README · What it looks like：`--html` writes one self-contained file — no scripts, no external assets — so a report can be
attached to a pull request, archived next to the session it describes, or opened from disk.

dsh-driftwatch README · What it measures：| Signal | Detail | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Tool sequence | LCS alignment: kept / removed / added, divergence % | 40% |
| Tool mix | per-tool count deltas across both runs | 25% |
| Metrics | records, turns, steps, messages, reasoning chunks/chars, compactions, retries, tool errors, max tools per turn | 20% |
| File targets | paths touched in only A / only B / both | 15% |

dsh-driftwatch README · What it measures：Those weights combine into a **0–100 drift score** with three tiers: `stable` (<10), `moderate` (10–34), `significant` (≥35).

DriftWatch never decides whether drift is *acceptable* — that judgment stays with you. The score and thresholds are just a way to make the change visible.
dsh-driftwatch README · CI integration：```yaml

dsh-driftwatch README · .github/workflows/drift.yml：- name: Behavior drift check
  run: |
    npx dsh-driftwatch compare "$BASELINE_SESSION" "$CANDIDATE_SESSION" \
      --fail-on-drift 35 --markdown drift-report.md
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  if: always()
  with:
    name: drift-report
    path: drift-report.md
```

`--json` emits the full machine-readable report (scores, deltas, file sets) for dashboards or PR bots.

dsh-driftwatch README · As a dsh plugin：Installing it into a profile also gives the agent two tools:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-driftwatch
```

| Tool | What the agent can do |
|---|---|
| `drift_compare` | compare two sessions and report the drift inline |
| `drift_list` | list available sessions to pick a baseline |

Useful for "compare how you did this task this time vs last time" — the agent gathers its own evidence.

dsh-driftwatch README · How the session log is read：DSH session logs are append-only `.jsonl.zstd`: every append is a separate zstd frame, so a log is a concatenation of frames. Node's zlib decodes only the first frame and its stream API rejects the rest; DSH itself relies on a private zstd handle plus a koffi FFI fallback.
section: How the session log is read

text: dsh-driftwatch README · How the session log is read：DriftWatch builds on **[`@edge-echo/dsh-ledger`](https://github.com/Edge-Echo/dsh-ledger)**, which parses the zstd frame structure (RFC 8878) instead of decompressing: 34,729 frames are located in **27 ms**, without decoding a byte, and boundaries are exact rather than recovered by retrying.
section: How the session log is read

text: dsh-driftwatch README · How the session log is read：The frame walk used to live here as a magic-scan heuristic, so the same subtle format was implemented twice. It now lives in one place, and the swap was checked rather than assumed: over a frozen 20 MiB log the old and new decoders produce the **identical 62,037,223-character payload and the same 53,671 records**. The structural walk costs about 17% more CPU in this path (overall time is dominated by zstd decoding, not by finding boundaries) — the win is exactness and one implementation, not throughput.
section: How the session log is read

dsh-driftwatch README · Limitations：- Session-log record types are read defensively: unknown types are ignored, missing fields are tolerated. A future format change degrades the report rather than crashing it.
- Sequence alignment is exact (LCS) up to 4 M cell pairs; beyond that it falls back to multiset overlap and says so in the report.
- DriftWatch compares *behavior*, not *correctness*. A stable run can be wrong; a drifting run can be better.
